EMG Report

  
Full Name:	Patient One	Gender:	Male
MR #:	000001	Date of Birth:	1/1/1981
Visit Date:	7/2/2026 3:18 PM

Examining Physician:	Dr. Andrew Colllins
Referring Physician:	Dr. Andrew Colllins
History and Exam: Mr. One is a 45 year old man who presents for re-evaluation of lower back pain, leg weakness, and paresthesias. EDX is performed for evaluation of lumbosacral radiculopathy.
 
Summary: 
The right median sensory nerve showed a prolonged latency, low amplitude, and slow conduction velocity. The right radial sensory nerve showed a low amplitude. The right sural nerve showed no response. All remaining sensory responses were normal.
The right median motor nerve showed prolonged latency and slowed conduction velocity in the forearm. The right peroneal motor nerve at the EDB showed prolonged latency and low amplitude. The right tibial motor nerve showed low amplitude and a conduction block below the popliteal fossa. All remaining motor responses were normal.
The right TA showed increased motor unit amplitudes and durations. The right Gastrocnemius showed increased insertional activity, abnormal spontaneous activity, reduced recruitment, and increased motor unit amplitudes and durations. The  showed increased insertional activity, abnormal spontaneous activity, reduced recruitment, and increased motor unit amplitudes and durations. The left Gastrocnemius showed increased insertional activity, abnormal spontaneous activity, reduced recruitment, and increased motor unit amplitudes and durations. All remaining muscles tested showed normal insertional activity, no abnormal spontaneous activity, normal motor unit amplitudes and durations, and normal recruitment patterns.

Impression: 
This is an abnormal electrodiagnostic study of the right upper, right lower, and left lower extremities which shows evidence of:
Acute on Chronic, bilateral lumbosacral radiculopathy of the L5 and S1 myotomes, with active denervation. 
A mild, length-dependent, axonal, sensory, large-fiber polyneuropathy; incidental finding.
A right, mild median neuropathy at the wrist, demyelinating. In this clinical context, this is consistent with a right, mild carpal tunnel syndrome.
In comparison with his previous 2025 study, there appears to be slight progression of the severity of denervated findings in his lumbosacral spine.

Summary

The sensory conduction test was performed on 4 nerve(s). The results were normal in 1 nerve(s): R Ulnar - Dig V (Antidromic). Results outside the specified normal range were found in 3 nerve(s), as follows:
In the R Median - Dig II (Antidromic) study
the peak latency result was increased for Wrist stimulation
the peak amplitude result was reduced for Wrist stimulation
the take off velocity result was reduced for Wrist - Index segment
In the R Radial - Superficial (Antidromic) study
the peak amplitude result was reduced for Forearm stimulation
In the R Sural - (Antidromic) study
the response was considered absent for Calf stimulation

The needle EMG examination was performed in 7 muscles. It was normal in 3 muscle(s): R. First dorsal interosseous, R. Vastus lateralis, L. Vastus lateralis. The study was abnormal in 4 muscle(s), with the following distribution:
insert was found in R. Gastrocnemius (Medial head), L. Tibialis anterior, L. Gastrocnemius (Medial head).
Abnormal spontaneous/insertional activity was found in R. Gastrocnemius (Medial head), L. Tibialis anterior, L. Gastrocnemius (Medial head).
vol act was found in R. Gastrocnemius (Medial head), L. Tibialis anterior, L. Gastrocnemius (Medial head).
The MUP waveform abnormality was found in R. Tibialis anterior, R. Gastrocnemius (Medial head), L. Tibialis anterior, L. Gastrocnemius (Medial head).
